## Step 1: Defining variables and General cleanup

-   ***Note that all DBH measurements are in cm unless otherwise
    stated!!!*** -tree conditions are coded 1-4: 1=healthy,
    2=LRR-symptom 3=LRR-dead, 4=other dead -treamtents are coded 1-3:
    1=unthinned, 2 and 3 are different thinning treatments with similar
    basal area but may vary in demography. -all plots are 1/10 acre,
    with 5 plots/stand = 0.5 acre inventoried/stand
-   Also note that all changes are being made to the "WC Final 2020 -
    08_05_20.xlsx" file. More specifically all changes are being made on
    the "original from everett" sheet.
-   Replaced all "x" with a blank space (made 1105 replacements).
-   Replaced all "?" with a blank space (made 5 replacements).
-   Changed 12D Tree #16 DBH from 2009 from 52.5 to 72.5 based upon
    2000 and 2020 DBH measurements (assumed data entry error from 2009).
-   Changed PLOT of 22B(ALT) to 22B (There were 25 replacements made).
-   Changed 11c Tree #20 2009 measurement from 15.1 to 75.1 based upon
    2000 and 2020 measurement (assumed data entry error).
-   Changed 11c Tree #30 2009 measurement from 36.4 to 56.4.1 based
    upon 2000 and 2020 measurement (assumed data entry error).
-   Changed 15B Tree #5 and 32A Tree #32, from "GC" to "CH" for
    Chinquapin
-   Added DBH measurements and tree health condition codes (THCC) from
    1990 "T2-B2" spreadsheet to "original from everett" sheet.
-   Combined measurements from 33E Tree #23 and 33E Tree#23* based
    upon context clues from notes and previous measurements matching
    closely to current measurements.
-   Removed tree 3 3 D 23 from dataset because no species code was ever
    assigned.

## Step 2: Check to Ensure that there are no measurements included within the data that have < 15.24cm DBH

-   ***Note that all DBH measurements are in cm unless otherwise
    stated!!!***
-   In excel sort by DBH starting with 1985 through 2020 (deleted 77
    trees).
-   In excel sort by DBH from 1985-2020 and delete any individual
    measurements from those years that were less < 15.24cm (edited 44
    trees).
-   Excel spreadsheet titled "edited_and_deleted_trees.xlsx" contains
    the records of all trees that were edited or deleted.

## Step 3: Removed trees with > 25 cm DBH if 2020 DBH was the only year where DBH was recorded

-   In excel sort by 2020 DBH (Removed 42 trees from the raw dataset).
-   Excel spreadsheet titled "edited_and_deleted_trees.xlsx" contains
    the records of all trees that were edited or deleted.

## Step 4: - Added condition codes for 2020 and double checked condition codes from other years.

-   Condition codes of 3 and 4 were not repeated and if DBH was recorded
    for the year where it was found to be 3 or 4 it was left but repeats
    were deleted to not include dead/snags/stumps/rotted wood etc. for
    more than one year.\
-   Made best judgement call on whether to include tree health condition
    code in 2020 for missing trees based upon notes from previous years.
    (If trees were missing and no notes were given for condition from
    previous years then condition code was left blank).
-   13B Tree #19 repeated the health condition code of 4 for 2009 and 3
    for 2020 since it was an eventual count for Laminated Root Root
    (code 3).
-   After consideration, there will be repeats of 3 and 4 codes but only
    on ORIG, 1985, and 1990. This is because for most analysis we will
    be using 1990 as the starting year since this is after the thinning
    occurred. However we might be using 1985 as a starting year
    therefore the repeats will be useful for the 1985 and or 1990
    analysis.

## Importing polished dataset to R for transposition, statistical analysis and visualization

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
#importing relevant sheet and columns from xlsx file and specifying variable types
WC_clean <- read_excel("~/WC_Final_2020_08_05_20_CLEANED.xlsx", sheet = "original from everett", range = "A1:W1808", col_types = c("text", "text", "text", "text", "text", "numeric", "text", "numeric", "text", "numeric", "text", "numeric", "text", "numeric", "text", "numeric", "text", "numeric", "text", "text", "text", "text", "text"))
#subsetting to remove "original" and "85" columns
drop<-c("ORIG DIA","ORIG COND","85 DIA","85 COND")
data_clean<-WC_clean[,!names(WC_clean) %in% drop]
#taking out trees with no species designation
data_clean<-subset(data_clean, is.na(data_clean$SPECIES)== FALSE)
#first checking that there are no rows with all NA conditions that may have been measured only before thinning.
data_clean_noNA<-data_clean[-(which(is.na(data_clean$`90 COND`)==TRUE & is.na(data_clean$`95 COND`)==TRUE& is.na(data_clean$`00 COND`)==TRUE&is.na(data_clean$`09 COND`)==TRUE&is.na(data_clean$`20 COND`)== TRUE)),]
```

```{r}
#attempt to fix ghosts without killing 2020 recruits
data_clean_noNA$`90 COND CUM`<-data_clean_noNA$`90 COND`
data_clean_noNA$`95 COND CUM`<-ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`90 COND CUM`==TRUE), data_clean_noNA$`95 COND`, ifelse(data_clean_noNA$`90 COND CUM`=="3"|data_clean_noNA$`90 COND CUM`=="4"|data_clean_noNA$`90 COND CUM`=="0", "0", ifelse((data_clean_noNA$`90 COND CUM`=="1"|data_clean_noNA$`90 COND CUM`=="2")&is.na(data_clean_noNA$`95 COND`)==TRUE, "4", data_clean_noNA$`95 COND`)))
data_clean_noNA$`00 COND CUM`<-ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`95 COND CUM`==TRUE), data_clean_noNA$`00 COND`, ifelse(data_clean_noNA$`95 COND CUM`=="3"|data_clean_noNA$`95 COND CUM`=="4"|data_clean_noNA$`95 COND CUM`=="0", "0", ifelse((data_clean_noNA$`95 COND CUM`=="1"|data_clean_noNA$`95 COND CUM`=="2")&is.na(data_clean_noNA$`00 COND`)==TRUE, "4", data_clean_noNA$`00 COND`)))
data_clean_noNA$`09 COND CUM`<-ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`00 COND CUM`==TRUE), data_clean_noNA$`09 COND`, ifelse(data_clean_noNA$`00 COND CUM`=="3"|data_clean_noNA$`00 COND CUM`=="4"|data_clean_noNA$`00 COND CUM`=="0", "0", ifelse((data_clean_noNA$`00 COND CUM`=="1"|data_clean_noNA$`00 COND CUM`=="2")&is.na(data_clean_noNA$`09 COND`)==TRUE, "4", data_clean_noNA$`09 COND`)))
data_clean_noNA$`20 COND CUM`<-ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`09 COND CUM`==TRUE), data_clean_noNA$`20 COND`, ifelse(data_clean_noNA$`09 COND CUM`=="3"|data_clean_noNA$`09 COND CUM`=="4"|data_clean_noNA$`09 COND CUM`=="0", "0", ifelse((data_clean_noNA$`09 COND CUM`=="1"|data_clean_noNA$`09 COND CUM`=="2")&is.na(data_clean_noNA$`20 COND`)==TRUE, "4", data_clean_noNA$`20 COND`)))
#comparing diameter distributions of live and dead trees throughout the study. Asking, are bigger trees more likely to die than smaller?
#first need to create a "terminal diameter" variable to capture the latest diameter measurement for each tree before/at death.
data_clean_noNA$term_dia<- with(data_clean_noNA, ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`20 DIA`)==FALSE, data_clean_noNA$`20 DIA`, ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`09 DIA`)==FALSE, data_clean_noNA$`09 DIA`, ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`00 DIA`)==FALSE, data_clean_noNA$`00 DIA`, (ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`95 DIA`)==FALSE, data_clean_noNA$`95 DIA`, ifelse(is.na(data_clean_noNA$`90 DIA`)==FALSE, data_clean_noNA$`90 DIA`, NA)))))))
#terminal diameter distribution of all trees, alive and dead
ggplot(data = data_clean_noNA, aes(x = term_dia)) + 
 geom_histogram(na.rm=TRUE)+ scale_color_viridis_d(na.translate = FALSE)+ xlab("Terminal DBH (cm)") + ylab("count")+ theme_classic()
#creating a binary "living" variable based on `20 COND CUM`
data_clean_noNA$living<-ifelse(data_clean_noNA$`20 COND CUM`==1|data_clean_noNA$`20 COND CUM`==2,"alive","dead")
#plot of terminal diameters for all trees
ggplot(data = data_clean_noNA, aes(x = term_dia, fill=living)) + 
geom_histogram()+ scale_fill_viridis_d()+ xlab("Terminal DBH (cm)") + ylab("count")+ theme_classic()
ggplot(data = data_clean_noNA, aes(x = term_dia)) + 
 geom_histogram()+ xlab("Terminal DBH (cm)") + ylab("count")+ theme_classic()+ facet_grid(~living)
#counts of living and dead trees
live_dead<-data_clean_noNA %>% group_by(living) %>% summarise(n())
live_dead
#persistent NAs
problem<-data_clean_noNA[which(is.na(data_clean_noNA$living)==TRUE),]

#write_rds(data_clean_noNA, "~/LeBoldus_Lab/Laminated_Root_Rot/data_clean_noNA.Rds")
```

```{r}
#pivoting data from wide to long format
#for diameters
long_data<- pivot_longer(data_clean_noNA, cols = c("90 DIA","95 DIA","00 DIA","09 DIA","20 DIA"), names_to = "YEAR", values_to = "DIA")
#for conditions
conds<-pivot_longer(data_clean_noNA, cols = c("90 COND","95 COND","00 COND","09 COND","20 COND"), names_to = "YEAR", values_to = "COND")
#for cumulative conditions
cum_conds<-pivot_longer(data_clean_noNA, cols = c("90 COND CUM","95 COND CUM","00 COND CUM","09 COND CUM","20 COND CUM"), names_to = "YEAR", values_to = "COND_CUM")
#combining
long_data$COND<-as.character(conds$COND)
long_data$COND_CUM<-as.character(cum_conds$COND_CUM)
#changing values to remove characters and then convert to numeric
#example : C_plots$TRT[C_plots$TRT=="DF0y"]<-"DF0Y"
long_data$YEAR[long_data$YEAR=="90 DIA"]<-1990
long_data$YEAR[long_data$YEAR=="95 DIA"]<-1995
long_data$YEAR[long_data$YEAR=="00 DIA"]<-2000
long_data$YEAR[long_data$YEAR=="09 DIA"]<-2009
long_data$YEAR[long_data$YEAR=="20 DIA"]<-2020
long_data$YEAR<-as.numeric(long_data$YEAR)
#subsetting to remove wide columns and irrelevant columns
drop2<-c("90 DIA","90 COND","95 DIA","95 COND","00 DIA","00 COND","09 DIA","09 COND", "20 DIA","20 COND","90 COND CUM","95 COND CUM","00 COND CUM","09 COND CUM","20 COND CUM", "living","13 COND","NOTES 2013")
long_data<-long_data[,!names(long_data) %in% drop2]
#creating unique tree ID variable of format TRT_BLOCK_PLOT_TREE
long_data$Tree_ID_TBP<-paste(long_data$TMT,long_data$BLOCK,long_data$PLOT,long_data$TREE, sep = "_")
#creating unique plot ID factor varaible of format TRT_BLOCK_PLOT
long_data$Plot_ID_TBP<-as.factor(paste(long_data$TMT,long_data$BLOCK,long_data$PLOT, sep = "_"))
#making proper factors while leaving year as a numeric variable 
long_data$TMT<-as.factor(long_data$TMT)
long_data$BLOCK<-as.factor(long_data$BLOCK)
long_data$PLOT<-as.factor(long_data$PLOT)
long_data$SPECIES<-as.factor(long_data$SPECIES)
long_data$YEAR_F<-as.factor(long_data$YEAR)
long_data$YEAR<-as.numeric(long_data$YEAR)
long_data$DIA<-as.numeric(long_data$DIA)
#designating trees as alive or dead in a given year (or not yet recruited) and calculating basal area of each tree and making new variables of diameters and basal areas for only living trees (cond 1 and 2)
#pasting either DIA for living or "0" for other cond values into live_DIA variable. function would not accept NA as "else" value. Then replacing "0" with NA
long_data$alive<-as.factor(if_else(is.na(long_data$COND_CUM)==TRUE, "<15cm", if_else((long_data$COND_CUM=="1"|long_data$COND_CUM=="2"), "Alive", "Dead")))
long_data$live_DIA<-if_else(long_data$alive=="Alive", long_data$DIA, 0)
#replacing 0 with NA
long_data$live_DIA[long_data$live_DIA==0]<-NA
#BA calcs
long_data$BA<-(long_data$DIA/200)^2*pi
long_data$live_BA<-(long_data$live_DIA/200)^2*pi
#making a more generic species lable of DF, HL, or other
long_data$species_gen <- as.factor(ifelse(long_data$SPECIES == "DF", "DF", ifelse(long_data$SPECIES == "HL", "HL", "other" ))) 
annual_live_count<-long_data %>% group_by(YEAR_F,alive, .drop = FALSE) %>% summarise(n())
annual_live_count_sp<-long_data %>% group_by(YEAR_F,species_gen, alive, .drop = FALSE) %>% summarise(n())
annual_live_count_plot<-long_data %>% group_by(Plot_ID_TBP,YEAR_F,alive, .drop = FALSE) %>% summarise(n())
annual_live_count_sp_plot<-long_data %>% group_by(Plot_ID_TBP,YEAR_F,species_gen, alive, .drop = FALSE) %>% summarise(n())
glimpse(long_data)
#write.csv(annual_live_count, file="~/LeBoldus_Lab/Laminated_Root_Rot/annual_live_count.csv")
#write.csv(annual_live_count_sp, file="~/LeBoldus_Lab/Laminated_Root_Rot/annual_live_count_sp.csv")
#write.csv(annual_live_count_plot, file="~/LeBoldus_Lab/Laminated_Root_Rot/annual_live_count_plot.csv")
#write.csv(annual_live_count_sp_plot, file="~/LeBoldus_Lab/Laminated_Root_Rot/annual_live_count_sp_plot.csv")
#write.csv(long_data, file="~/LeBoldus_Lab/Laminated_Root_Rot/long_data.csv")
#write_rds(long_data, "~/LeBoldus_Lab/Laminated_Root_Rot/long_data.Rds")
```

```{r}
#summarizing mean live diameter over time by treatment
mean_DIA_df <- long_data %>%   
  group_by(TMT, YEAR_F, .drop = FALSE) %>%  
  summarise(live_DIA_mean=mean(live_DIA, na.rm = TRUE), live_DIA_se=sd(live_DIA, na.rm = TRUE)/sqrt(n()), n_samples = n())%>% ungroup()
glimpse(mean_DIA_df)
#converting factor year back to numeric and restoring values for plotting
mean_DIA_df$YEAR<-as.numeric(mean_DIA_df$YEAR_F)
mean_DIA_df$YEAR[mean_DIA_df$YEAR==1]<-1990
mean_DIA_df$YEAR[mean_DIA_df$YEAR==2]<-1995
mean_DIA_df$YEAR[mean_DIA_df$YEAR==3]<-2000
mean_DIA_df$YEAR[mean_DIA_df$YEAR==4]<-2009
mean_DIA_df$YEAR[mean_DIA_df$YEAR==5]<-2020
#plotting mean live diameter
ggplot(data = mean_DIA_df, # add the data
       aes(x = YEAR,  #set x, y coordinates
           y = live_DIA_mean,
           color = TMT)) +    # color by treatment
  geom_point(size = 3) + # set size of the dots
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin= (live_DIA_mean - live_DIA_se), ymax= (live_DIA_mean + live_DIA_se)))
```

## Step 5: Formating the Spreadsheet for FVS

-   Using the spreadsheet titled "WC Final 2020 - 08_05_20_CLEANED"
    which has been edited from the raw data file "WC Final 2020 -
    08_05_20" by following the steps from above we will now use it to
    format the datasheet for use within FVS.
-   In excel the 90 DIA column was convereted from "cm" to "inch" using
    the CONVERT function.
-   All tree health condition codes were converted as follows to fit the
    FVS model history parameters field:

Current "History" coding conversion for 1990 is:

| Our code | FVS conversion |
|----------|----------------|
| 1        | 1              |
| 2        | 5              |
| 3        | 6              |
| 4        | 6              |

-   Code 1 = 1 (Healthy = Live Tree)
-   Code 2 = 5 (Symptomatic = Live tree)
-   Code 3 = 6 (Recently dead)
-   Code 4 = 6 (Recently dead)

"Tree history codes of 0-5 are used to represent live tree records that
are projected by FVS. FVS does not distinguish between the various live
tree codes. Tree history codes 6, 7, 8, and 9 indicate types of tree
records that are not projected."
<https://www.fs.fed.us/fmsc/ftp/fvs/docs/gtr/EssentialFVS.pdf>

## Step 7: Setting the Western Root Disease Parameters

| Dam | Sev   | Model        | Comments  |
|-----|-------|--------------|-----------|
| 62  | 00-03 | Root Disease | Phellinus |

Severity codes are defined as follows:

-   01 = Tree is within 30 feet of a root disease infected tree

-   02 = Symptoms of root disease detected on the tree

-   03 = Symptoms of root disease and crown deterioration detected

If the severity code is 01 and the tree diameter is not more than 5
inches, then the tree is regarded as an uninfected small tree in the
disease center; if the severity code is 00 or 01 and the tree diameter
is greater than 5 inches, the tree is regarded as an infected large
tree\

When it comes to specifying disease centers, there are two schools of
thought on this and it really depends on the overall root disease
condition in the stand. If there are identifiable root disease pockets
or centers, you can some those up for the stand for the number of
centers. If the diseased trees, live and dead, are basically scattered
throughout the stand, a single center is the best choice. In defining
parameters with the RRInit keyword, the percent of roots infected (a
pathologist would give a much better estimate) 0.1 (10%) is considered
light infection and mortality will occur well before 100% of roots
become infected depending on the disease type. Specification of infected
and uninfected number of trees does not need to be specific tree counts,
because the model is just using these values to calculate a proportion.

-   Dam code of 62 for all trees that had signs/symptoms (severity code

    2)  or mortality (severity code 03).

-   If the plot center tree was infected then every tree within that
    plot was coded with a 00,01 for that year.

-   If tree was coded with a 02 or 03, an estimation of proximity was
    done and the previous two trees and the next two trees within the
    plot were assigned with a 00.

-   If last tree in the plot was coded a 02 or 03 then trees #1 and #2
    were coded with a 01 and vice versa if the last two trees within the
    plot were coded as 02 or 03.

"When root disease occurs in numerous small centers or when the edges of
centers are not readily discernible on the ground, the stand should be
modeled as one disease center."
(<https://www.fs.fed.us/rm/pubs/rmrs_p054/rmrs_p054_055_067.pdf>)
